claims.text: The 'Gen. Arthur S. Trudeau' named in the 1955 FBI material quoted in philip-corso.narrative is most probably this officer. Reasoning: the two primary letters opened here give the middle initial G over his own signature, and no second Army general officer of that surname was found. The discrepancy is unresolved and no record opened here reconciles it.

edges.label: Two Directors of Central Intelligence corresponded with him in office
edges.note: Two Directors of Central Intelligence corresponded with him in office, Dulles in January 1958 on avoiding duplication between CIA and Army research programmes and McCone in March 1962 on the Limited-War Mission symposium.

edges.label: Corso's Foreign Technology Division chieftaincy falls inside Trudeau's tenure
edges.note: Corso's DA Form 66 places his Foreign Technology Division chieftaincy, 18 April to 18 July 1962, inside Trudeau's documented tenure as Chief of Research and Development.

edges.label: Addressed at the Department of the Army, Washington 25, D. C.
edges.note: Both letters address him at the Department of the Army, Washington 25, D. C.
